items.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: I did a lot of live television work. I did a lot during the 60s and 70s, there must have been eight or ten musical variety shows on the air. There was Dean Martin and Carol Burnett, Sonny & Cher, Jack Benny, Red Skelton

ctx.x: Wow. It must have been, just from a logistical standpoint too, I picture like leaving all those instruments in your car all day if you didn’t use them.

Yeah, it was a problem. I had what they call a space blanket, it was like a thin, it looked sort of like aluminum foil with another kind of backing that would help to keep them from overheating. I put this over all these guys you know. So that was hard work, but it paid well, because doubling paid well, in particular in recording work and motion picture work and film/television work. The doubling didn’t pay as well in live television. I did a lot of live television work. I did a lot during the 60s and 70s, there…
How did that work from a set up standpoint? Where was the band as opposed to the actors and actresses?
